subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Why EVs Skip the Gearbox
description: A quick win: understand Why EVs Skip the Gearbox.

hook.text: Electric cars usually have just one gear. No shifting, no clutch, no torque converter.

buildup.text: A gas engine makes power in a narrow RPM band and needs gears to stretch it across speeds.

discovery.text: Electric motors deliver full torque from zero RPM and stay efficient across a wide speed range.

twist.text: That's why EVs feel so fast off the line—instant torque with no gear changes to interrupt.

climax.text: Some performance EVs like the Porsche Taycan use two gears for even more top speed efficiency.

punchline.text: Electric motors are so flexible they barely need gears.

quiz.question: Why do most EVs have only one gear?
options: Electric motors deliver torque across all speeds

details.summary: Electric motors produce strong torque from zero RPM across a wide speed range, eliminating the need for a multi-speed gearbox. Most EVs use a single fixed-ratio reduction gear instead.
details.whyItMatters: Removing the complex gearbox simplifies the EV drivetrain, reducing weight, maintenance costs, and mechanical failures while delivering seamless, jerk-free acceleration at any speed.
takeaways: Electric motors deliver peak torque instantly from standstill
A single reduction gear replaces the multi-speed transmission
Fewer moving parts mean lower maintenance and longer life

faq.question: Would a multi-speed gearbox make an EV faster?
faq.answer: Potentially at very high speeds where motor efficiency drops. Porsche uses a two-speed gearbox in the Taycan for this reason, but for most driving conditions a single gear is sufficient and simpler.

faq.question: Why can't combustion engines work with a single gear like EVs?
faq.answer: Combustion engines produce usable torque only across a narrow RPM band. Without multiple gears, they would stall at low speeds or over-rev at high speeds. Electric motors have no such limitation.
